original_clauses.source_paraphrase: At launch, Fable 5 redirected elementary biology and ordinary medical-science prompts to Opus 4.8; Anthropic said the safety filters were intentionally conservative and blocked most biology-work queries while false positives were reduced.
original_clauses.recovered_invariant_interpretation: A restricted-domain trigger should track the risk-relevant content or use condition closely enough that benign subject membership does not itself remove access to the selected capability; here the deliberately broad trigger creates an unresolved activation-validity boundary.

taxonomy_relationships.rationale: Anthropic described the broad biology routing as a deliberate safety trade-off: benign biology prompts fell within the intentionally broad launch trigger. The evidence therefore does not establish that the control became operative while its own valid activation conditions were unsatisfied; overbreadth or disproportionate policy scope alone is excluded from FC-000043.
The public evidence does not establish a classifier confidence state, required assurance threshold or downstream reliance rule sufficient to prove epistemic reliance miscalibration.

original_clauses.source_paraphrase: The redirect visibly identified the switch to Opus 4.8 and allowed users to continue on that model instead of leaving the request blocked.
original_clauses.recovered_invariant_interpretation: When a restriction applies to one capability, users should be able to distinguish the restricted model from the available fallback and continue through that route where it remains appropriate.

taxonomy_relationships.rationale: Anthropic visibly distinguished Fable 5 from the Opus fallback and reran affected requests on that alternative, preserving the model-state and continuation path under the biology gate.

original_clauses.source_paraphrase: Anthropic later reported that Fable 5.1 intervened on benign biology requests 85 percent less often than the launch safeguards.
original_clauses.recovered_invariant_interpretation: A safeguard adjustment should reduce unnecessary restriction while maintaining the protective purpose; the reported false-positive reduction does not by itself establish the revised control’s miss rate or complete effectiveness.
